A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same signSGD study. Their main text, equations, figures, table, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and the added minibatching material.

before.justification: V2 reports original synthetic-data simulations and CIFAR10/IMDB experiments in Figure 1, plus dimensionality, learning-rate, and conditioning experiments in Appendix D.

after.justification: V3 retains those experiments and adds minibatch simulations with Rademacher noise in Figure 5.

M1.justification: Equation (1) extends single-sample signSGD to applying the sign function after averaging a minibatch. The corresponding signHSGD drift gains batch-dependent factors. The regression objective and underlying preconditioning structure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Figure 5 adds optimizer simulations under Rademacher label noise, previously examined through analytical compression-factor plots. The existing Gaussian/Cauchy synthetic experiments and CIFAR10/IMDB tasks are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged, including SGD/vanillaODE and the signHSGD/signODE predictions. The minibatch sweep introduces no new competing optimizer; Appendix D adds an analytical SDE comparison.

E3.justification: The new Figure 5 sweeps batch sizes 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, and 100 with learning-rate compensation for batch size. Existing experimental settings, including Table 1, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 5 adds a batch-size sensitivity analysis testing the theoretical approximation and whether minibatching alleviates poor small-risk behavior under Rademacher noise. Earlier dimensionality, learning-rate, and conditioning analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The existing 80% confidence intervals and disclosed counts of 20 synthetic-data runs and 50 CIFAR10 runs are unchanged. Figure 5 specifies no additional run counts, seeds, confidence levels, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: New Figure 5 reports simulation/theory agreement and lower limiting risk with larger batches under its compensated learning rates. All earlier plot data and reported experimental values are retained; these are additional results, not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Definition 2 and Appendix D substantially extend the mathematical formulation through batch-dependent noise, scaling, and SDE comparisons. V3 also revises noise regularity and initialization conditions, tightens the moment conditions in Theorems 1–2, and changes several equations and proof steps. The displayed main proof still uses batch size 1.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and concluding discussion retain the same central claims: high-dimensional risk approximations, four effects distinguishing signSGD from SGD, and a heuristic extension toward Adam.

C2.justification: Section 5 introduces interpretations of minibatching as smoothing effective label noise and approaching Gaussian behavior when the noise has finite variance. It also connects batch scaling to learning-rate compensation and distinguishes numerical minibatch validation from the main theorem's single-sample setting.

D1.justification: Figure 5 documents batch sizes and learning-rate compensation for the new experiment. Existing hardware, numerical solvers, preprocessing, noise fitting, Table 1 settings, and code-access information are retained in Appendix I, previously Appendix H.

R1.justification: The historical discussion replaces Kushner and Clark (1978) with Robbins and Monro (1951), with the corresponding bibliography substitution. Positioning relative to concurrent weak-approximation work and earlier high-dimensional SGD research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 adds a minibatching section and appendix, an impact statement, and expanded acknowledgments. It makes localized wording and terminology edits and fixes unresolved Figure 4 references. Most retained prose and the narrative sequence remain stable.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from one column to two, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. Figure 3's panels become vertically stacked, Table 1 is reformatted, and the new minibatching plot becomes Figure 5. Earlier plots are retained under the revised layout and numbering.

improvement.justification: V3 adds useful minibatch validation and mathematical corrections, including Equation (21). However, new Equation (10) gives N_1 = 1/pi although Definition 2 gives 1. Revised Equation (222) also changes phi(R_t) to phi(2R_t), further diverging from the retained main ODE. These mathematical inconsistencies affect the quantitative analysis, making the net benefit of the extension and corrections uncertain.
